title: Non-vanishing away from the origin for Fourier-transformed tautological systems of very ample equivariant line bundles on projective homogeneous spaces
source_title: Tautological systems, homogeneous spaces and the holonomic rank problem
author: Paul Görlach; Thomas Reichelt; Christian Sevenheck; Avi Steiner; Uli Walther
difficulty_reason: The standard homogeneous-space and D-module prerequisites do not determine when the cyclic right-module construction vanishes after passage to its twisted anticanonical description. The authors supply the full local Lie-algebroid kernel/tensor-power and equivariant-line-bundle vanishing arguments, then combine their source-specific torsion and monodromy geometry with fiber inversion to obtain the exact necessary-and-sufficient tensor-power condition. This remains a substantive new construction and global criterion after the ordinary reductive-group, Kodaira/Picard and D-module foundations are allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem4.34, with Section4.4 assumptions: smooth projective X with transitive action of a connected reductive complex algebraic group G, very ample G-equivariant L, V=H0(X,L)^dual, and Gprime=Cstar times G acting inversely on fibers. Lie character beta vanishes on g; positive k satisfies pi1(Lstar)=Z/kZ. The Fourier-transformed tautological module restricted to V minus the origin is i-prime-plus O_(Lstar)^(ell/k) exactly when beta(e)=ell/k and L^ell is G-equivariantly isomorphic to omega_X^(-k); otherwise this restriction vanishes. The embedding i-prime includes fiber inversion Lstar to Ldual,star, so its sign convention is preserved. No assertion about the origin-supported part or general nonhomogeneous spaces. Full local new closed-embedding description28–31, Lie-algebroid vanishing/twist module32–41, homogeneous big-cell and line-bundle geometry41–44, rank-one monodromy and necessary-and-sufficient condition44–46 read. Fundamental group/local-system construction10–12 and authored Fano support52–54 read. Named standard reductive-group, Kodaira/Fano, Picard and D-module background is traced in the original. Later localization, mixed-Hodge structure and full holonomic-rank outcomes remain unselected and their cores are not certified. Entire74-page original retained with actual JEP13(2026), DOI10.5802/jep.332 and pinned source dates.
